## Cause

`fastify()` is an overload set. The two HTTP/2 overloads (`FastifyHttp2Options`, `FastifyHttp2SecureOptions`) declare `http2: true`, while the HTTPS and plain HTTP overloads (`FastifyHttpsOptions`, `FastifyHttpOptions` in `fastify.d.ts:67-79`) didn't mention `http2` at all. So `http2: false` (or `undefined`) matched no overload: `false` isn't assignable to `true`, and for the http/https overloads `http2` was an excess property.

## Fix

Added `http2?: false` to both `FastifyHttpsOptions` and `FastifyHttpOptions` in `fastify.d.ts`, so an explicit `false`/`undefined` selects the http (or https) overload and the instance is typed with `http.Server`/`https.Server`. Added matching assertions to `test/types/fastify.tst.ts`.

## Verification

`tstyche` isn't installed in this checkout, so `npm run test:types` can't run here. I verified with the vendored `tsc` (`--strict`, `node16` resolution) against a scratch file that now type-checks clean:

- `fastify({ http2: false })` → `FastifyInstance<http.Server, …>`
- `fastify({ https: {}, http2: false })` → `FastifyInstance<https.Server, …>`
- `fastify({ http2: undefined })` → http instance
- `fastify({ http2: true })` / `fastify({ http2: true, https: {} })` still resolve to `Http2Server` / `Http2SecureServer`
- the existing negative cases `fastify<http2.Http2Server>({ http2: false })` and `fastify<http2.Http2SecureServer>({ http2: false })` still error (their `@ts-expect-error` directives remain satisfied), since neither HTTP/2 server type extends `http.Server`

One note on the report: the narrow `false` literal means a variable of type `boolean` (e.g. `http2: config.USE_HTTP2 === true` assigned to a `boolean` field, rather than a literal comparison inlined at the call site) still won't pick an overload — overload resolution can't produce a server type that depends on a runtime value. That case needs a branch (`USE_HTTP2 ? fastify({ http2: true }) : fastify({})`) or `as const`. The reported `false`/`undefined` cases are fixed. Nothing committed.
